Format SCF Regression Model Results for APA-Style Table Rendering

Source: R/scf_extract_model.R
scf_extract_model.Rd

Extracts and formats model output from SCF regression functions (scf_ols(), scf_glm(), etc.) into a clean two-column table suitable for publication-style display. Coefficients and standard errors are combined into APA-style cells, significance stars are applied, and common fit statistics (R-squared, AIC) are appended. Output is structured to support table-joining across multiple models.

scf_extract_model(model, model_name = "Model", latex = TRUE, multiline = FALSE)

Arguments

model

A regression output object in tidy data frame format, typically returned by scf_ols(), scf_glm(), or scf_logit().

model_name

A character string indicating the model column label (e.g., "Model 1a"). This becomes the column name in the returned table.

latex

Logical. If TRUE, underscores in variable names are escaped (\\_) for LaTeX output. Default is TRUE.

multiline

Logical. If TRUE and latex = TRUE, coefficient and SE are stacked on separate lines using LaTeX \\ linebreaks. Requires LaTeX makecell package. Default is FALSE.

Value

A tibble with two columns: label (term names) and the user-specified model_name column. The model column contains formatted coefficient entries in the style: 0.123** (0.045). Fit statistics (R-squared, AIC) are appended as additional rows at the bottom.

Details

This function is typically used to prepare model summaries for kable(), stargazer(), or other publication-quality workflows. When latex = TRUE, formatting is applied to ensure compatibility with LaTeX typesetting, including escaping underscores and optional multiline rendering via \\.

Coefficients are rounded to 3 decimal places and accompanied by standard errors in parentheses. Significance stars are added using the following conventional thresholds:

  • *** if p < 0.001

  • ** if p < 0.01

  • * if p < 0.05

  • ^ if p < 0.10

If the input model lacks a stars column, it will be generated automatically from p.value.

Use Case

This function is especially useful when displaying multiple SCF models side-by-side. Tables can be joined on the label column to construct multi-column comparison tables. Pair with dplyr::full_join() or purrr::reduce() for model stacking.

See also

scf_ols(), scf_glm(), scf_logit(), scf_MIcombine()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
model1 <- scf_ols(scf2022, log_networth ~ education1 + age1)
table1 <- scf_extract_model(model1, model_name = "Model 1a")
knitr::kable(table1)
} # }
